title: Microhedge slab reallocation and price gradient prototype (May 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working prototype for a small, targeted hedge ("microhedge") that reallocates committed slab credits across customer segments and couples the reallocation with a graduated pricing gradient to manage unit economics while preserving gross usage. The goal: buy 3–6 months of improved margin flexibility without a full price replate or a broad hiring freeze.

Context / why this exists:
- We are seeing token demand concentration in a handful of mid-market customers while spot/on-demand demand is growing in lower-commitment tiers.
- GPU spot and quantization savings projections give us ~6–12% per-token cost upside if we accelerate quantization and KV-cache rollout.
- Leadership wants a low-friction lever that preserves product velocity for high-value customers but recovers margin if demand growth accelerates unpredictably.

High-level hypothesis:
If we reassign a modest portion of slab/reserved capacity to a "microhedge pool" (2–6% of committed GPU tokens) and implement a 3-band price gradient for on-demand and trial tiers, we can preserve ~>50% of incremental margin at low churn risk while providing predictable headcount breathing room.

Key assumptions (working):
- Blended current per-token revenue: $0.0008/token (weighted across routes).
- Blended current per-token variable cost: $0.00042/token (GPU time, networking, storage, amortized infra).
- Quantization & runtime improvements (fast path + 4-bit Q) could reduce variable cost by 9% if adoption reaches 40% of workload in 90 days.
- Price elasticity: short-term (0–90d) elasticity for on-demand customers estimated at -0.6; for trials and low-touch tiers -1.1 (higher sensitivity).
- Hiring plan: we were planning +12 FTEs through Q4 (avg fully loaded comp $230k/year).

Simple scenario sketches (tokens/month basis):

Scenarios (monthly incremental) | Price delta | Demand delta | Unit cost delta | Margin delta (pp) | Headcount impact
Base                          | 0%          | 0%           | 0%              | 0                 | +12 planned
Conservative (microhedge)      | +4%         | -6%          | -2% (quant opt) | +2.1 pts           | defer 3 hires
Aggressive repricing           | +12%        | -25%         | -2%             | -1.4 pts           | freeze +6 hires
Discount push (retain growth)  | -8%         | +30%         | +1%             | -0.2 pts           | accelerate hires if revenue positive
Notes on table: margin delta approximated as (price change - cost change) * elasticity-weighted demand. These are order-of-magnitude checks, not model outputs.

Mini-sheet: headcount phasing + cost (annualized run-rate view)
Role | Current FTEs | Planned hires (H2 2026) | Avg fully loaded comp | Annual incremental delta
Eng (serving/runtime) | 38 | +5 | $260,000 | $1,300,000
SRE/Infra             | 12 | +3 | $240,000 | $720,000
Product / PD          | 9  | +2 | $200,000 | $400,000
Finance / Ops         | 6  | +1 | $180,000 | $180,000
Support / CS          | 16 | +1 | $150,000 | $150,000
Total planned hires: 12 -> incremental annual comp ~$2.75M (on payroll).

Runway sensitivity (simplified):
- Current cash cushion allocated to ops: $42M (cash runway baseline ~14 months at current burn).
- If we defer 3 hires and execute microhedge, we save ~ $690k/year (~0.2 months runway), plus expected variable cost savings from quantization (projected $1.1M/year if adopted).
- Conservatively, microhedge + partial quantization buys ~3–4 months of operating flexibility when combined with modest price gradient.

Pricing gradient prototype (3 bands, external-facing):
1) Core (enterprise + reserved): unchanged pricing; keep committed SLAs and dedicated capacity allocation.
2) On-demand standard: +4% list price for new usage above per-account baseline; grandfather existing consumption for 30 days.
3) Trial / low-touch: implement a tiered discount & throttle policy. New trial volumes see -8% price cap for first 30 days, then step to on-demand base (protects conversion flow).
Why a gradient? reduces churn risk in high-value segments while nudging marginal usage price on the elastic buckets.

Pricing sensitivity quick calc example (monthly incremental 100M tokens across segments):
- If 40M tokens are on on-demand band: +4% price -> +$12.8k rev; demand drops 6% -> -2.4M tokens = -$7.68k; net +$5.12k (~0.5% uplift on that bucket).
- If trial bucket (20M) gets -8% introductory -> conversion increases but short term rev drops by ~$12.8k; we assume lifetime conversion +40% offsets in 180d horizon.

Risk register (quick):
- Customer upset / PR risk from perceived stealth price changes (mitigate: 30d notice + grandfathering + clear comms).
- Elasticity misestimate: trial bucket could churn more than predicted (mitigate: pilot on 10 accounts first).
- Quantization rollout lags (mitigate: gating save assumptions by Q3 readiness).

Operational playbook (90d run):
Week 0: align legal on messaging & contract language; prepare API flags for price gradient; pick pilot cohort (top 10 mid-market and 20 low-touch). Owner: Noah Rivera.
Week 1–2: implement billing flags + telemetry to track token delta by customer cohort. Owner: Finance eng (Evelyn).
Week 3–6: enable microhedge pool rules (reallocate up to 5% of slab credits to microhedge). Observe queueing latency and SLA telemetry. Owner: Tomás.
Week 6–12: pilot on small cohort; collect churn/conversion signals; run quick margin P&L. Decision gate at day 60: expand / rollback. Owner: Exec: CFO + Head of Product.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need better short-window price elasticity estimates for top-20 on-demand accounts. (owner: growth analytics)
- Confirm legal on contract amendment approach for slab reallocation. (owner: legal)
- Build a small dashboard showing per-account token elasticity, margin delta, latency SLO delta. (owner: observability)

Decision criteria for scaling microhedge beyond pilot:
- Net margin improvement > 1.2% normalized across account cohorts AND
- No SLA degradations beyond 99.95% monthly target AND
- Net churn attributable to pricing change < 0.8% of pilot ARR.

Notes to self (raw):
- This is intentionally conservative on demand drop; better to under-predict short-term lift.
- If quantization achieves 12% variable cost drop we can be bolder on on-demand price; if only 3–4% we should keep gradient tight.
- Consider coupling microhedge with a small usage credit (one-time) for strategic accounts as a churn soak.

Appendix: simple model cell examples (for modeling team copy/paste)
- current_rev = tokens * price_per_token
- new_tokens = tokens * (1 + elasticity * price_delta)
- new_rev = new_tokens * (price_per_token * (1 + price_delta))
- cost_savings = old_cost_per_token * tokens * cost_delta
- net_margin_delta = new_rev - new_cost - (old_rev - old_cost)

If this prototype looks reasonable, next step is to convert the mini-sheet above into a sanitized worksheet (sensitive account ids removed) and run the pilot simulation across the top 50 accounts for a 90-day projection.

-- End of working draft --
